title: Design a safe heat-exchanger experiment
equipment: Plate heat exchanger with steam-side valve and product outlet-temperature transmitter
physicalPurpose: Collect informative local response data without exceeding the reviewed valve and product-temperature envelope.
objective: Design, review, execute, abort, and restore one bounded heat-exchanger step experiment before accepting identification data.

simplifications: Local first-order-plus-dead-time response at one operating point
No steam-pressure, flow, fouling, sensor, valve, or product-property variation
Direct simulated actuator after the requested-versus-applied clamp

baseline.limitation: Constant data are uninformative and an unreviewed excitation may be unsafe or causally ambiguous.

change.decision: Collect data only after plan bounds, baseline qualification, aborts, restoration, evidence class, and approval boundary are explicit.

acceptance.window: first to last sample of 10 s baseline
final 10 s of qualified 63 s excitation

abortPredicates: Outlet-temperature quality is bad or stale
The authorised operating mode is lost
Product temperature or valve position leaves its declared envelope
safety.restorationMode: Restore 60 percent valve and wait until product temperature is within 0.1 degC of baseline
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised process controls engineer and plant operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The shipped project cannot authorise or execute physical I/O
Physical use requires independently reviewed topology, interlocks, safe state, operator coordination, and explicit approval immediately before excitation

video.viewerOutcome: Design and execute a bounded simulation experiment, reject an unsafe plan, and prove abort plus restoration.

learning.context: A steam-side valve controls product outlet temperature on a plate heat exchanger near a declared operating point.
learning.reason: An unknown model requires informative data, while an arbitrary excitation can be unsafe, too short, or confounded.
theory: An experiment asks one engineering question and holds other causal inputs sufficiently steady.
Baseline, excitation amplitude, duration, limits, abort conditions, restoration, evidence class, and approval are designed before collection.
Simulation approval never authorises a physical valve movement.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict 55 degC for Plan A at 70 percent valve for 63 seconds and reject Plan B because 85 percent valve predicts 62.5 degC.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, signals, units, quality, mode, 100 ms sampling, disturbance state, limits, and safe restoration.
Record the prediction and review decision before Start.
learning.baseline: Show that constant data are uninformative and that an unreviewed plan has no authority to excite the plant.
learning.change: Review and execute the bounded 10-point simulation step, then repeat it with an injected quality failure.
learning.comparison: Compare rejected, qualified, and aborted plans using defined baseline, excitation, prediction, constraint, and restoration measures.
learning.validation: Require Plan B to leave the valve unmoved, Plan A to match its prediction within 0.35 degC, and bad quality to abort and restore without qualified identification data.
learning.explanation: A bounded single-input experiment supports causal interpretation, while rejection and abort protect the operating envelope and evidence integrity.
learning.transfer: Lesson 38 compares excitation shapes because one safe step cannot expose every relevant dynamic.
